data.title: What Investors Got Wrong About Indosat Before The Drop
data.description:
Indosat looked like a telecom set up for steady AI cloud expansion and network upgrades, yet the scorecard for 2026 tells a different story. Investors who held Indosat from the start of the year are down 36.7%, including dividends. If you had been weighing that decision on 1 January, with consensus expecting revenue growth of 6.6% and a profit margin near 10.9% within three years, what exactly did that original thesis fail to factor in?

A Narrative on Simply Wall St is one investor's written case for a company, with its growth, margin and multiple assumptions spelled out. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

The Two Indosat Stories Investors Were Arguing Over

The shares cost IDR2,320 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Indosat then had to choose between two very different but reasonable stories.

On the optimistic side, the bullish narrative put fair value at IDR2,642 and focused on AI cloud services plus network upgrades. In that view, Indosat was assumed to grow revenue 6.6% a year and increase profit margin to 10.9% within three years.

The bearish case anchored on a fair value of IDR1,600 and emphasized shrinking legacy voice and SMS revenues, where over the top apps were expected to keep pressuring high margin services and overall profitability.

What The Results Changed For The Indosat Argument

The Q3 2026 update gave investors one hard fact to work with. Indosat reported revenue of IDR14,051,989m and net income of IDR612,864m, compared with IDR14,051,989m and IDR1,252,096m a year earlier. Net margin moved from 8.9% to 4.1%. That challenged the optimistic thesis that higher AI cloud and network spending would quickly lift profitability.

The main lesson is simple. When a story leans on margin expansion, investors need to track the reported net margin line every quarter and check whether it is actually moving closer to the stated target.

Indosat trades at IDR1,425 today, with shareholders down 36.7% from the start of the year. The selected Narrative still places Fair Value above that level, framing the gap around a mix of AI Neocloud, fibre monetisation and tighter cost control.

data.title: Nippon Sanso Holdings Corporation (TSE:4091) Half-Yearly Results: Here's What Analysts Are Forecasting For This Year
data.description:
Last week saw the newest interim earnings release from Nippon Sanso Holdings Corporation (TSE:4091), an important milestone in the company's journey to build a stronger business. The result was positive overall - although revenues of JP¥737b were in line with what the analysts predicted, Nippon Sanso Holdings surprised by delivering a statutory profit of JP¥82.88 per share, modestly greater than expected. This is an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance in its report, look at what experts are forecasting for next year, and see if there has been any change to expectations for the business. With this in mind, we've gathered the latest statutory forecasts to see what the analysts are expecting for next year.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Following last week's earnings report, Nippon Sanso Holdings' eight analysts are forecasting 2027 revenues to be JP¥1.47t, approximately in line with the last 12 months. Statutory per-share earnings are expected to be JP¥331, roughly flat on the last 12 months. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of JP¥1.47t and earnings per share (EPS) of JP¥331 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

View our latest analysis for Nippon Sanso Holdings

There were no changes to revenue or earnings estimates or the price target of JP¥6,213, suggesting that the company has met expectations in its recent result. Fixating on a single price target can be unwise though, since the consensus target is effectively the average of analyst price targets. As a result, some investors like to look at the range of estimates to see if there are any diverging opinions on the company's valuation. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Nippon Sanso Holdings at JP¥7,600 per share, while the most bearish prices it at JP¥4,800. Analysts definitely have varying views on the business, but the spread of estimates is not wide enough in our view to suggest that extreme outcomes could await Nippon Sanso Holdings shareholders.

Another way we can view these estimates is in the context of the bigger picture, such as how the forecasts stack up against past performance, and whether forecasts are more or less bullish relative to other companies in the industry. We would highlight that Nippon Sanso Holdings' revenue growth is expected to slow, with the forecast 2.9% annualised growth rate until the end of 2027 being well below the historical 8.0% p.a. growth over the last five years. By way of comparison, the other companies in this industry with analyst coverage are forecast to grow their revenue at 5.4% per year. Factoring in the forecast slowdown in growth, it seems obvious that Nippon Sanso Holdings is also expected to grow slower than other industry participants.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that there's been no major change in sentiment, with the analysts reconfirming that the business is performing in line with their previous earnings per share estimates. Fortunately, the analysts also reconfirmed their revenue estimates, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Although our data does suggest that Nippon Sanso Holdings' revenue is expected to perform worse than the wider industry. There was no real change to the consensus price target, suggesting that the intrinsic value of the business has not undergone any major changes with the latest estimates.

Following on from that line of thought, we think that the long-term prospects of the business are much more relevant than next year's earnings. We have forecasts for Nippon Sanso Holdings going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here.

Personalis (PSNL)

Personalis uses high depth genomic sequencing plus AI driven analytics to help oncologists and drug developers detect residual cancer earlier and fine tune treatment decisions. This positions the company within the broader healthcare AI theme.

Personalis, Inc. develops AI enabled cancer genomic tests like NeXT Personal and ImmunoID NeXT for MRD detection, tumor profiling and pharma research, and has a market cap of about US$1.69b.

"Expanding Medicare coverage for NeXT Personal in breast and lung cancer surveillance, along with active submissions for IO monitoring and neoadjuvant breast cancer, points to a larger pool of reimbursed tests that could lift clinical revenue and support margin recovery from current low levels."

One relatively quiet shift in how these AI driven tests are paid for could potentially change the economics of Personalis much faster than currently anticipated.

Insmed (INSM)

Insmed leans on a growing respiratory medicines franchise today, while its AI driven protein engineering work hints at a very different drug design toolkit tomorrow. This is why it earns a spot in an AI focused healthcare screen.

"Continued expansion of BRINSUPRI into the growing diagnosed U.S. bronchiectasis population of at least 500,000 patients, with company guidance for more than $1.25 to $1.4b in 2026 BRINSUPRI revenue and a raised peak sales view of more than $7b, points to further potential scaling of Insmed revenue and operating leverage."

What happens to that operating leverage if a single assumption about how quickly new patients come onto treatment proves too optimistic?

Insmed develops treatments for serious and rare diseases, with respiratory drugs like ARIKAYCE driving its US$1.52b in rare disease therapy revenue, and an AI driven protein engineering program targeting future medicines on top of a roughly US$23.9b market value.

If that patient ramp risk is what you keep circling back to, read the full narrative for Insmed to see how Insmed’s AI work could accelerate or cushion the story.

Mettler-Toledo International (MTD)

Mettler-Toledo International leans heavily on precision instruments, but its LabX software and AI driven imaging tools quietly turn raw lab readings into cleaner, faster decisions for diagnostics and drug research, which is exactly why it earns a place in an AI healthcare screen.

Mettler-Toledo International Inc. supplies precision instruments and lab software that support diagnostics, drug R&D and quality control, with AI linked LabX and imaging layered on top of a broad hardware base. Revenue is spread across U.S. Operations at about US$1.63b, Western European Operations at roughly US$1.14b, Swiss Operations at around US$1.08b, Chinese Operations near US$1.01b and Other Operations at about US$870 million. The group has a market value of roughly US$34.53b.

"Expanding bioprocessing and broader biopharma activity, including facility expansions, GLP‑1 manufacturing and reshoring related investments, is expected to create further demand for Mettler Toledo International’s process analytics and industrial equipment along the biopharma value chain."

data.title: Earnings Miss: M3, Inc. Missed EPS By 14% And Analysts Are Revising Their Forecasts
data.description:
M3, Inc. (TSE:2413) came out with its half-year results last week, and we wanted to see how the business is performing and what industry forecasters think of the company following this report. It was not a great result overall. While revenues of JP¥182b were in line with analyst predictions, earnings were less than expected, missing statutory estimates by 14% to hit JP¥16.38 per share. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We've gathered the most recent statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their earnings models, following these results.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Taking into account the latest results, the most recent consensus for M3 from twelve analysts is for revenues of JP¥388.2b in 2027. If met, it would imply a credible 7.1% increase on its revenue over the past 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to ascend 11% to JP¥77.03. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of JP¥388.2b and earnings per share (EPS) of JP¥77.03 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

View our latest analysis for M3

There were no changes to revenue or earnings estimates or the price target of JP¥1,969, suggesting that the company has met expectations in its recent result. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. There are some variant perceptions on M3, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at JP¥2,850 and the most bearish at JP¥1,600 per share. This is a fairly broad spread of estimates, suggesting that analysts are forecasting a wide range of possible outcomes for the business.

Looking at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can make sense of these forecasts is to see how they measure up against both past performance and industry growth estimates. We can infer from the latest estimates that forecasts expect a continuation of M3'shistorical trends, as the 15% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2027 is roughly in line with the 13% annual growth over the past five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in a similar industry are forecast to see their revenues grow 11% per year. So although M3 is expected to maintain its revenue growth rate, it's definitely expected to grow faster than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that there's been no major change in the business' prospects in recent times, with the analysts holding their earnings forecasts steady, in line with previous estimates. Happily, there were no major changes to revenue forecasts, with the business still expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at JP¥1,969, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. We have forecasts for M3 going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here.
